season_context.local_season_notes: Cold, grey winters from November to March favour coats, knitwear, boots and layering. Christmas markets and gifting in December drive sales, followed by end-of-season markdowns in January. Berlin Fashion Week runs in late January/early February, and Munich Fabric Start in July and January sets the textile direction. SS27 enters stores from February.

sources.title: Herbst/Winter 2026: Diese Modetrends erobern die Geschäfte

trends.name: Plush, loop-yarn and brushed textures
trends.summary: German stores are stocking shaggy plush knits, brushed surfaces, loop yarns, fuzzy cotton and terry details. Volume and tactility are treated as a deliberately sensual statement.

trends.name: Neo-gorpcore and 90s outdoor
trends.summary: Outdoor classics are updated for city wear, with archive technical sportswear from brands such as Nike and K-Way becoming hybrid everyday pieces. Zalando's German trend hub also lists neo-gorpcore.

trends.name: Chocolate brown
trends.summary: Zalando Germany names a rich chocolate brown as its colour of the season, alongside an animal print edit and layered autumn looks.

trends.name: Boxy leather jacket
trends.summary: Leather jackets come in boxy, slightly relaxed cuts with structured shoulders, in smooth clean leather, replacing tight traditional fits.

trends.name: Tartan, Glencheck and windowpane
trends.summary: Checks appear on oversized coats, tailored skirts and shirts. In menswear they come back in larger, textured versions that feel less traditionally British.

trends.name: Menswear: knit vest over long shirt
trends.summary: German stylists recommend sleeveless chunky-knit vests worn over shirts with a clearly visible hem, plus thick roll necks and plain wool coats styled with faded jeans for a less polished look.

trends.name: Slimmer, relaxed men's suiting
trends.summary: Oversized looks are fading. Men's suits are narrower, often with pleated trousers and a tie, but are worn with sneakers or sturdy boots and don't need to match.

trends.name: Red replaces burgundy in menswear
trends.summary: Brown, camel and olive remain the menswear base, while red from signal red to deep wine takes over as the accent. Wine-red leather blousons with shearling collars are a key piece.

trends.name: Brooches and sheer pieces for men
trends.summary: Sheer tops, deep necklines and sequins are entering men's collections, and brooches are flagged as a menswear accessory likely to grow in coming seasons.

trends.name: Crystal and pearl embellishment on daywear
trends.summary: Crystal and pearl appliqués are migrating from evening dresses to everyday garments to lift them, and sheer layering continues from summer into practical silhouettes.

trends.name: Oktoberfest: tonal, apron-free Tracht
trends.summary: Wiesn 2026 favoured tonal brown and burgundy outfits, dirndl dresses without aprons, chain belts, two-piece bodice sets with capri trousers, velvet Miesbach vests, sheer blouses and matching children's Tracht.

trends.name: Two-piece dirndls with mesh blouses
trends.summary: Separable blouse-and-skirt dirndls, high-necked mesh blouses replacing lace, velvet and shimmering jacquard, and dark midnight blue, wine and olive tones led the 2026 dirndl season. Adidas launched a sporty dirndl.

trends.name: Kids' Tracht mirroring adult looks
trends.summary: Children's traditional wear for the 2026 Wiesn matched adult styles, with authentic outfits for both boys and girls instead of costume-like versions.

trends.name: Protective, forward-leaning outerwear
trends.summary: Berlin AW26 favoured guarded shapes. John Lawrence Sullivan used forward-set sleeves and rounded backs, Dagger showed baggy, imperfect proportions, and elongated oversized coats compressed the upper body.

trends.name: Black, ice metallics and crimson
trends.summary: Black anchored Berlin AW26, with sparing silver and snow-white metallics, crimson on shoes and jackets, and faded denim blues, greys and earth tones.

trends.name: Reuse and repair as design method
trends.summary: Buzigahill rebuilt second-hand garments into 60s and 70s East African shapes, and Kenneth Ize layered aso oke with velvet, denim and lining fabrics with seams left visible.

trends.name: Berlin grunge, skate and DIY
trends.summary: Berlin SS27 brought grunge back. Dagger mixed ripped baggy denim, Hawaiian shirts, tie-dye and star prints, Unvain showed red leather and low-rise jeans, and DIY cut-outs and laced tees were widespread.

trends.name: Graphic prints, tie-dye and 3D-printed surfaces
trends.summary: Dagger relied on printed stars, yin-yang, tie-dye, camo and lipstick-kiss graphics. Kasia Kucharska used 3D printing to warp pastel shirting and add squiggly textures to latex trenches.

trends.name: GmbH's polished sport-tailoring
trends.summary: For its tenth anniversary, GmbH paired technical sportswear with precise tailoring and added reflective and metallic finishes, subtle sequins and glossy equestrian boots for a more luxurious Berlin look.

trends.name: Coverage-led pleats at William Fan
trends.summary: William Fan's SS27 collection centred on coverage and inclusive cuts, with flowing pleated silhouettes, ruffs, extra-long sleeves and layering in a restrained palette.

trends.name: Sculptural volume and blurred gender codes
trends.summary: Berlin SS27 featured voluminous skirts with trains at Rebekka Ruétz, low-crotch wide trousers at Milk of Lime, and Renaissance breeches with tailcoats at Marke. Men's and women's codes increasingly overlapped.

trends.name: Imperfect denim and crinkle textures
trends.summary: Munich Fabric Start's SS27 edition made imperfection the denim theme. Heat-shrunk yarns create crinkle, colourful flock prints add interest, and digitally printed denim-look twill replaces washes. Lace, embroidery and loop yarns are gaining.

trends.name: Yellow and orange for summer 2027
trends.summary: Fabric suppliers at Munich Fabric Start expect a range of yellow and orange shades to lead summer 2027 colour.

trends.name: TASTE: heritage classics and non-synthetic stretch
trends.summary: Munich Fabric Start's July 2026 AW27/28 theme, TASTE, revived British heritage, outdoor folklore and functional tailoring. It highlighted deep atmospheric colours and stretch without synthetic fibres, plus cashmere-silk blends and new lyocell types.

trends.name: Menswear grey-black-blue with muted orange-yellow
trends.summary: For AW27/28 menswear, Munich exhibitors built the palette on grey, black and blue with a muted orange-yellow accent, along with brushed shirting, brown and olive tones and blurred prints.
